# analyzer

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/immutago/pkg/analyzer"
```

Package analyzer exposes the immutago go/analysis analyzer.

Structs that embed im.Shared or im.Scoped are immutable from construction. Their fields must be scalars, unnamed arrays, other marked structs, pointers to concrete Shared structs, or frozen collections of allowed types. Each component is checked recursively. Unmarked structs cannot store protected values. Interfaces, callbacks, and user generics with protected storage are unsupported. Ordinary unsafe and reflection operations follow Go API contracts.

Whole variable bindings can be replaced. Field, element, and pointer\-target writes to protected objects are rejected. Protected pointers start with fresh construction and target concrete marked structs. Shared pointers can be copied, stored, and returned. Scoped pointers stay local or pass to direct typed calls that do not retain them. Neither mode permits protected closure captures or protected operations in go or defer.

Struct and array copies copy their values; frozen fields share read\-only storage. Freeze calls consume exclusive native map and slice builders without copying. Builder aliases and later uses are rejected; Clone creates independent native storage. Direct im or supervise imports, locally used im or supervise type contracts, and failed checked dependencies select proof checking. Other packages use ordinary Go API trust, including string immutability. Checked failures propagate to consumers.

Supervised services have a separate source boundary. The analyzer matches the exact Service, Ref, and startup identities from package supervise. Callers keep a Ref and use Current only for a direct exported method call. Exported method inputs and outputs must be allowed stored types. Service receivers can access their mutable fields, but cannot escape their methods. Start arguments may contain explicit ConcurrentSafe values whose concurrency promise is not proved.

## Variables

Analyzer checks immutable type obligations and reports unsupported aliasing and mutations.

```go
var Analyzer = &analysis.Analyzer{
    Name:      "immutago",
    Doc:       "prove immutability of marked structs and immutable collection elements",
    Run:       run,
    FactTypes: []analysis.Fact{new(invalidPackage)},
}
```
